findings.title: totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size
findings.body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so a group with exactly 100 members and limit 50 reports 3 pages instead of 2. Because showingLast compares currentPage to this inflated totalPages, the Next control stays enabled on the real last page and the next action advances offset to 100, where findMembers returns an empty member list. The page count and pagination state are therefore wrong for every exact-multiple group size.

findings.title: Members endpoint accepts unbounded, zero, and negative limit/offset values
findings.body: limit and offset are taken directly from params with only to_i and no clamping. A caller who can view a group can pass limit=1000000 to force loading and serializing an arbitrarily large member set in one request, pass limit=0 (which also makes the client's totalPages divide by zero), or pass a negative offset/limit, which raises a database error and returns a 500. The endpoint should clamp limit to a sane range (e.g. 1..some max) and offset to >= 0.

findings.title: Public group members page silently truncates membership to the first 50 users
findings.body: findMembers now always requests the default limit of 50 members, and GroupsController#members now applies that limit to all groups (previously non-automatic groups returned their full member list and automatic groups defaulted to 200). The public template discourse/templates/group/members.hbs renders `members` with no pagination controls, unlike the new admin UI, so for any group with more than 50 members the remaining members are unreachable from the public members page.

findings.title: Group creation silently discards the alias_level sent by the client
findings.body: The client's Group.asJSON() sends alias_level and the group form shows the alias-level combo-box even for a not-yet-saved group, but Admin::GroupsController#create only assigns name and visible before saving. Any alias level chosen while creating a group is silently lost and the group is created with the default alias_level; only editing and re-saving afterwards sets it. Create should assign params[:alias_level] like update does.

findings.title: findMembers clamps offset to user_count, landing on an empty page after the last member of a page is removed
findings.body: The requested offset is clamped with Math.min(user_count, offset). Removing the sole member shown on the last page (e.g. offset 50 of 51 members) triggers removeMember -> findMembers while user_count is still the stale 51, so offset 50 is requested even though only 50 members remain, and the server returns an empty page with total 50. Combined with the inflated totalPages, the admin is left staring at an empty page instead of being moved back to the previous page; the clamp should be based on the last valid page start, not user_count.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses PUT although only DELETE is routed
findings.body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but config/routes.rb only routes DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member and the JavaScript client uses DELETE. Controller specs dispatch directly to the action and bypass routing, so this test passes even if the DELETE route or verb handling were broken, and it documents the wrong verb for the endpoint. It should use :delete like the neighbouring removal example.
